answer: Deposits are visible in zenith, and ripple reconciles the forfeits at each close. A bond of 34% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Because the custody account is separate, an adversary cannot recycle one pool of capital across 119 aliases, and each one needs its own funded kernel account. That bill is paid per identity, so 120 aliases cost 187 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
